findings.title: Satisfaction borne by the life-state
findings.claim: The satisfied outcome is grammatically borne by the life-state itself, so the recipient's judged worth can be perceived as a condition that fits him rather than only as a pleasure he possesses.
findings.mechanism: The focus adjective رَّاضِيَةٍ is an active qualifier agreeing with عِيشَةٍ, while the wider 88:9 occurrence ties the same satisfaction wording to completed striving. The focus life noun therefore becomes the carrier of an attained, fitting condition for the resumed person in فَهُوَ.
findings.reader_payoff: The result becomes a lived condition aligned with the person's outcome, while the plain sense of being in a pleasing life remains fully recoverable.
findings.containment: The Arabic surface and focus morphology establish the agreement; the wider connection is used as a semantic parallel without importing its unavailable target morphology. This does not claim literal emotion in a life or remove the ordinary reading of a pleasing life.

epistemic.reason: The focus carrier and agreement are supplied directly and the cross-run finding is trusted, while the corroborating reader walk is legacy_unbound and the wider target's morphology is not supplied.

findings.title: A life that receives its inhabitant

findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the outcome as a meeting between person and condition, not only as a thing awarded to him.
findings.containment: The focus form is an active feminine participle, not an explicit reciprocal construction. The mutuality is therefore an attributed, qualified inference supported by the paired external wording; the ordinary favorable-life reading remains intact.

epistemic.reason: A trusted publication and exact focus relation support the finding, while the reader-walk corroboration is legacy_unbound and the reciprocal force is inferred rather than morphologically explicit.
